input.reason: The claim concerns physical optical terminals remaining available during severe local cloud cover — a real-world atmospheric/hardware phenomenon. No registered checks exist that cover this claim. The two available runners (emulated-netem-v1 and real-world-iperf-v1) can measure TCP/UDP flow completion times over emulated or real IP links, but neither can induce or measure actual cloud-cover-induced optical link attenuation/availability. There is no available equipment (e.g., FSO terminals, weather instrumentation, cloud-cover sensors), no real-world optical testbed, and no dataset of optical link availability under cloud cover. The source is a synthetic text-only evaluation packet with no real paper, so there are no author-provided datasets or configurations to draw from. No prospective pilot can be responsibly proposed without physical optical hardware and environmental control or measurement capability. The claim is therefore blocked on missing equipment, missing data, and missing implementation.

blockers.detail: No free-space optical (FSO) or physical optical terminal hardware is available. The claim requires actual optical link hardware whose availability can be measured under cloud-cover conditions.
blockers.required_input: Physical FSO or optical ground terminal hardware with telemetry output (link availability/attenuation logs) accessible to a registered runner.

blockers.detail: No cloud-cover or atmospheric attenuation dataset is available. Verifying availability under 'severe local cloud cover' requires either real-time weather/cloud sensor data co-located with the optical terminal, or a historical dataset of link availability vs. cloud-cover events.
blockers.required_input: Time-series dataset of optical link availability (up/down state or received power) paired with co-located cloud-cover measurements (e.g., oktas, satellite imagery, ceilometer data) during severe cloud events.

blockers.detail: Neither emulated-netem-v1 nor real-world-iperf-v1 can model optical link physics (cloud-induced attenuation, scintillation, beam blockage). Emulating cloud cover as a netem loss/delay profile would not constitute a valid test of physical optical terminal availability.
blockers.required_input: A registered runner or validated simulation framework capable of modeling FSO link availability under cloud-cover conditions, or direct integration with a physical optical testbed.
